FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides and Pesticides Residue Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Phosphamidon, technical, which is systemic in action, is employed in the preparation of insecticidal formulation for the control of sacking, mining and chewing insect pests and acarine pests of agricultural crops. Phosphamidon is the accepted common name by the International Organization for Standardization (1S0) for the systemic insecticide containing 2-chloro-2-diethylcarbamoyl- 1-methylvinyl dimethyl phosphate. The empirical formula and structural formula and molecular mass of phosphamidon are given below:
Empirical Formula CH30 Structural Formula Molecular Mass

Taking into consideration the views of producers, consumers, testing authorities and technologists, the Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard felt that it should be related to the manufacturing practices followed in the country in this field. This standard is one of a series of India mStandardson pesticides and their formulations. In preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the"Rulesframed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides Act and Rules, wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

ANNEX A

DETERMINATION A-O GENERAL OF PHOSPHAMIDON ACTIVE INGREDIENT CONTENT

Either of the two methods, namely, high performance Iiquid chromatographic (HPLC) and Iodometric methods may be used for determining active ingredient content. However, in case of dispute HPLC method shall be the referee method. A- I IODOMETRIC METHOD

A-1. 1 Outline of the Method Phosphamidon along with by-products reacts with iodine in strongly alkaline solution consuming four equivalents of iodine. The by-products, but not phosphamidon, consume iodine in sodium carbonate solution. The differential titration thus gives the content of phosphamidon. A-1.2 Reagents A-1.2.1 Standard Sodium Hydroxide Solution -- 2 N.
A-1.2.2 Standard Sodium Carbonate Solution --2 N.

a 250-ml iodine flask. Add, while stirring, 20.0 ml of the standard iodine solution. Then add 20-ml of the standard 2N sodium hydroxide solution. Shake well and set aside in the dark at 25 &2�C for 30 min. Acidify the mixture with 20 ml of the standard 5 N hydrochloric acid solution and titrate the excess iodine with the standard O.IN sodium thiosulphate solution using starch solution as the indicator. The end point is given by the discharge of blue colour. Note the value of titre (A ml). Carry out a blank with the same quantities of the reagents. Note the value of titre (J'ml). A-1.3.3 Pipette out 10.0 ml of the stock solution into another 250-ml iodine flask. Add, while stirring, 5.0 ml of the standard iodine solution. Then add 5 ml of the -standard 2N sodium carbonate solution. Shake well and set aside in the dark at 25 + 2�C for 15 m-in.Acidify the mixture with 5 ml of the standard 5 N hydrochloric acid solution and titrate as above with the standard 0.1 N sodium thiosulphate solution using starch solution as the indicator. Note the value of titre (B ml). Carry out a blank with the same quantities of the reagents. Note the value of titre (U ml). A-2.4.2 Preparation of Test SampIe Solution

Weigh (to the nearest of 0.1 mg) into a volumetric flask (250 ml) sufficient sample to contain 100 mg of phosphamidon (W,). Dissolve and dilute it up to the mark with mobile phase.
A-2.4.3 System Equilibration

A-2 HIGH PERFORMANCE LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPHIC METHOD A-2.1 Outline of the Method

Inject 10 ml of the reference standard solution till areas of phosphamidon peak from two consecutive injections agree to 1 percent maximum.
A-2.4.4 Determination

Phosphamidon is determined by reverse phase high-pressure liquid chromatography. Test sample of phosphamidon is compared with phosphamidon reference standard and percentage of phosphamidon is estimated by external standard method. A-2.2 Apparatus A-2.2. 1 HPLC System Liquid chromatography equipped with injector (10 p 1 loop), high sensitivity UV detector and suitable electronic integrator. A-2.2.2 Chromatographic Column--RP-18; particle size: 5 p m; length: 250 mm; inner diameter: 4.6 mm or equivalent.
A-2.2.3 A-2.2.4 A-2.2.5 A-2.2.6 A-2.3 A-2.3.1

Make duplicate 10 ml injections of the sample solution, followed by injection of standard sample. Average the areas of the injections following and preceding the sample injection (A,). Record the relevant peak areas of the sample (At).
A-2.4.5 Guide Values

Retention time : 4.8 min (phosphamidon peak) Run time

(see Note). : 21 min.

Eluent Flow Rate -- 1ml/min. Temperature -- Ambient. Injection Volume -- 10 ml, fixed loop.
Detector Reagents Acetonitrile -- HPLC grade. Wavelength -- 220 nrn.

NOTE -- Phosphamidon peak may split(isomer separation) depending upon the condition of analytical column. In that case add both the peak areas for calculation purpose. Retention time is an indicative parameter that may change slightly from time to time.

Review of Indian

Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and' Standards: Monthly Additions'.
